proof: Each translated cell x+V has centroid x and identical area alpha.
Expanding |(x-g)+z|^2 and integrating z over centrally symmetric V kills the cross term.
The intrinsic cell contribution is N*J_V. For a regular hexagon of circumradius 1/sqrt(3), mean r^2=5/36, hence J_V=alpha*5/36=5*sqrt(3)/72.
theorems.statement: Let V be the triangular-lattice Voronoi cell (area alpha=sqrt(3)/2, centered polar moment J_V=5*sqrt(3)/72). For any N-cell cluster C and its Voronoi union Omega_C, the centroid of Omega_C is g(C), and J(Omega_C;g(C)) = alpha*I2(C)+N*J_V = alpha*G(C)/N+N*J_V. Hence at fixed N, minimizing G is exactly equivalent to minimizing the continuum polar second moment over admissible Voronoi unions.

proof: Write E=Omega\D and F=D\Omega; both have area m=|Omega Delta D|/2.
Among outside subsets of area m, int_E (r^2-R^2) is minimized by the adjacent outer annulus and equals m^2/(2*pi).
Among inside subsets removed with area m, int_F (R^2-r^2) is minimized by the adjacent inner annulus and equals m^2/(2*pi).
Adding gives moment excess >= m^2/pi = |Delta|^2/(4*pi). Equality at zero symmetric difference yields the disk.
theorems.statement: For any measurable planar set Omega of area A with centroid g, and the equal-area disk D=B(g,R), J(Omega;g)-A^2/(2*pi) >= |Omega symmetric_difference D|^2/(4*pi).

proof: Let S_m={x in Lambda:Q(x)<=m}, and choose the least integer m with |S_m|>=N. Keep every site with Q<=m-1 and enough Q=m sites to obtain exactly N.
Every nonzero lattice site has a nearest-neighbor step of strictly smaller Q, so the inner sublevel is connected and every retained Q=m site attaches to it.

S_m is hole-free because every site with Q>m has a nearest-neighbor step of strictly larger Q leading to infinity; deleting unused outer-shell sites cannot create a hole because each deleted shell site has an outward Q-increasing neighbor already in the exterior.

With triangular-lattice covering radius d=1/sqrt(3), the Voronoi union contains B(0,sqrt(m-1)-d) and is contained in B(0,sqrt(m)+d). Minimality of m and fixed area A=N*sqrt(3)/2 imply sqrt(m)=Theta(sqrt(N)) and the equal-area disk radius lies between these radii up to O(1).

Therefore symmetric-difference area is O(sqrt(N)); multiplying the O(sqrt(N)) boundary-strip area by O(N) squared-radius scale gives O(N^(3/2)) moment discrepancy. Re-centering at the union centroid can only lower polar moment.
theorems.statement: There exists, for every N, a connected hole-free N-cell cluster T_N whose Voronoi union differs from its equal-area Euclidean disk by O(sqrt(N)) area and has polar-moment excess O(N^(3/2)).

theorems.forbidden_inference: This post-freeze theorem does not make Euclidean disk, radius, or pi part of D1/D2 move selection.
proof: PF-T01 transfers fixed-N G minimization exactly to polar-moment minimization among admissible Voronoi unions.
PF-T03 supplies an admissible comparison with disk moment plus O(N^(3/2)), while PF-T02 supplies the disk lower bound and quantitative stability.
Since A=Theta(N), moment excess O(A^(3/2)) and PF-T02 imply |Delta|=O(A^(3/4)); dividing by A gives O(A^(-1/4))=O(N^(-1/4)).
theorems.statement: For any choice C_N^* of global G minimizer at each N, let Omega_N be its Voronoi union, translated to its own centroid, and D_N the equal-area disk. Then |Omega_N Delta D_N|/|Omega_N| = O(N^(-1/4)) -> 0. Thus global G minimizers have a disk limit in normalized symmetric-difference measure, even if finite-N minimizers are not unique.

proof: The frozen centered-shell theorem gives H_r as a D1 strict local minimum for every r>=1. The rescaled axial sets H_r={max(|a|,|b|,|a+b|)<=r}, and hence their Voronoi unions up to an O(1) boundary thickening, converge to the regular hexagon defined by that axial unit ball.
Every global G minimizer is necessarily a D1 terminal state, because any strict D1 decrease would contradict global minimality.
PF-T04 shows any sequence of global G minimizers converges to the Euclidean disk in normalized symmetric difference.
A Euclidean disk and regular hexagon are distinct positive-symmetric-difference shapes after equal-area normalization, so the two terminal subsequences are genuinely different.
theorems.statement: The family of D1 terminal states has no unique rescaled limit shape: one subsequence converges to a regular hexagon and another converges to a disk.
